description: Adds target_customer_origin to the interpreter output contract, extends the location_needs block with three new needs, and defines the activation rules that connect interpreted intent to the new scoring layer. Merge into the existing schema by section.

enum_additions.note: These four values are exhaustive and mutually exclusive as categories. A business may draw from multiple origins — hence the weighted structure. Weights must sum to 1.0.

output_template_additions.section: Add these fields to the output_template object alongside existing fields

items.origin: one of: resident | daytime_worker | destination_visitor | passing_traffic

target_customer_origin.purpose: Declares the origin mix of the primary customer base. Drives which tract indicators are weighted in fit scoring. Must be populated by the interpreter from business description and priority_text signals.
target_customer_origin.fallback_if_ambiguous: Use the default weights from business_families_cluster_patch.json for the matched business_family_id. Flag in interpretation_notes that defaults were applied.

location_needs_additions.section: Add these three fields inside location_needs in the output_template

activation_signals: priority_text contains: upscale, luxury, premium, high-end, boutique, exclusive, prestige
business description implies high ticket price or brand co-location logic
business_family_id is retail_storefront and description mentions specialty or artisan positioning
user explicitly states target customer is high-spend
luxury_cluster_fit.activation_logic: If any activation signal is present, set to a value between 0.6 and 0.95 depending on signal strength. If no signal is present, set to 0.0 — do not default to a non-zero value.
luxury_cluster_fit.independence_note: This is independent of affluent_area. Both may be non-zero simultaneously. Never set one based on the value of the other.

activation_signals: Any business concept where co-location logic matters (most families except warehouse and trade-office)
User mentions 'near other shops like mine', 'good neighborhood for this type', 'established area for X'
business_family_id has non-empty synergistic list in cluster_affinity
compatible_business_cluster.activation_logic: Default to 0.5 for all business families with meaningful cluster_affinity data. Set higher (0.7-0.9) when the business concept is explicitly cluster-dependent (luxury retail, restaurant row, wellness strip, creative district, professional services hub). Set lower (0.2-0.3) for back-office or logistics operations.
compatible_business_cluster.independence_note: This is not a replacement for footfall or visibility. It specifically measures quality-of-cluster, not quantity of traffic.

activation_signals: business description mentions: lunch crowd, office workers, B2B, corporate clients, weekday demand
business_family_id is one of: food_beverage_quickservice, professional_office_service, digital_creative_studio
business_family_id is food_beverage_sitdown with daytime orientation

mandatory_activation.rationale: These three families have daytime_worker as their dominant customer origin. Failing to activate this need for them produces systematically incorrect location scores.

daytime_worker_concentration.activation_logic: For mandatory families, set to minimum 0.6 regardless of explicit user signals. For other families, activate (0.4-0.8) when target_customer_origin daytime_worker weight >= 0.25. Set to 0.0 only when daytime_worker weight is below 0.15.
daytime_worker_concentration.independence_note: This is not the same as affluent_area or demand_score. A high daytime_worker_concentration in a tract with average residential income is a real and valid signal. Do not suppress it based on income indicators.

interpreter_activation_rules.description: Rules the interpreter must apply to set the three new location_needs fields. These are deterministic — not judgment calls.

rule_1_luxury_cluster_fit.condition: priority_text OR business_text contains any luxury signal keyword
rule_1_luxury_cluster_fit.action: Set luxury_cluster_fit to 0.75 (moderate signal) or 0.90 (strong/explicit signal). Add to interpretation_notes: 'Luxury cluster fit activated based on premium positioning signal in description.'

rule_2_compatible_business_cluster.condition: business_family_id has non-empty synergistic list AND is not warehouse_logistics_fulfillment or home_property_trade_service_office
rule_2_compatible_business_cluster.action: Set compatible_business_cluster to 0.5 as baseline. Adjust upward if cluster_dependency_signals are present.
cluster_dependency_signals: User mentions wanting to be 'near similar businesses'
Business concept is a destination type (luxury, specialty, wellness)
business_family_id is one of: bar_nightlife_entertainment, professional_office_service, health_medical_therapy, digital_creative_studio, workshop_maker_light_production

rule_3_daytime_worker_concentration.condition: business_family_id in mandatory list OR target_customer_origin daytime_worker weight >= 0.25
rule_3_daytime_worker_concentration.action_mandatory: Set daytime_worker_concentration to minimum 0.6. Add to interpretation_notes: 'Daytime worker concentration mandatory for this business family — LEHD office worker data is the primary tract signal for this concept.'
rule_3_daytime_worker_concentration.action_conditional: Set daytime_worker_concentration to 0.4 + (0.4 * daytime_worker_weight). Example: daytime_worker weight 0.40 → daytime_worker_concentration = 0.4 + (0.4 * 0.40) = 0.56.

example_output_delta.description: Shows only the additions to the existing wine bar example — not a full replacement
example_output_delta.business_text: small evening wine bar with tapas
interpretation_notes_additions: luxury_cluster_fit not activated: no premium positioning signal detected in description.
compatible_business_cluster set to 0.75: wine bar has strong synergistic affinity with food_beverage_sitdown and bar_nightlife_entertainment — cluster quality matters significantly for this concept.
daytime_worker_concentration set to 0.30: after-work transition demand is real but secondary to evening destination draw — daytime_worker weight 0.25 triggers conditional activation.

example_output_luxury_contrast.description: Contrasting example: upscale ballet shoe boutique — shows how the same business_family_id produces very different need scores based on positioning signals
example_output_luxury_contrast.business_text: ballet and dance shoe boutique, premium brands, target serious dancers and dance schools
example_output_luxury_contrast.priority_text: upscale, specialty — not a mass-market shoe shop
interpretation_notes: luxury_cluster_fit activated at 0.80: explicit premium signal in priority_text ('upscale, specialty').
compatible_business_cluster set to 0.85: this concept depends on proximity to dance studios, performing arts venues, and arts education — synergistic cluster is a primary viability condition.
footfall reduced to 0.30 vs standard retail_storefront 0.85: destination_visitor pattern means customers travel specifically — passive street footfall is not the draw.
daytime_worker_concentration set low at 0.10: target customer is a dancer or dance school buyer, not an office worker.
This illustrates a core distinction: two retail_storefront businesses can have radically different location logic based on positioning.
